visual_symptoms: Uniform pale light-green to general chlorosis of older leaves starting from leaf tip and progressing along midrib; stunted tillering.
similar_conditions: Bacterial leaf streak, early leaf blast chlorosis, or general root rot.
soil_association: Coarse textured sandy soils, leached floodplains, low organic carbon (<0.5%).
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Top-dress with Urea or apply 1-2% foliar spray of Urea early morning for rapid greening.

visual_symptoms: Characteristic yellowing starting at leaf tip and progressing in an inverted V-shape along central midrib, leaving margins green longest.
similar_conditions: Drought firing, root rot, or northern corn leaf blight at early stage.
soil_association: Sandy soils, poorly drained Vertisols during high rainfall.
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Foliar spray of 2% Urea or side-dress with Ammonium Sulphate / Urea as per soil test.
source: ICAR-IIMR & UAS Bangalore Package of Practices

visual_symptoms: Leaves appear dark green with distinct bronze or purplish discoloration along margins; narrow, short, erect leaves; severely restricted tillering.
similar_conditions: Tungro virus leaf discoloration, iron toxicity bronzing.
soil_association: Acidic soils of Kerala and Coastal Karnataka (pH <5.5) or calcareous soils of Rayalaseema/TN (pH >8.0).
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Basal application of phosphatic fertilizer; in standing crop, foliar spray of 1% Diammonium Phosphate (DAP) or 0.5% 13-0-45.
source: KAU Package of Practices & ANGRAU Vyavasaya Panchangam

visual_symptoms: Leaves turn dark dull green with intense purple or reddish-violet pigmentation on veins and undersides of leaves and stems; poor root development.
similar_conditions: Tomato spotted wilt virus (TSWV), cold temperature physiological purpling.
soil_association: Red sandy loams of South India with low available Olsen-P (<10 kg/ha).
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test

visual_symptoms: Yellowish-white mottling between veins followed by marginal chlorosis; leaf tips and margins curl downwards and scorch (marginal necrosis / firing); leaves turn reddish-bronze.
similar_conditions: Alternaria leaf spot, Verticillium wilt marginal necrosis, parawilt.
soil_association: Red sandy soils (Alfisols) and weathered soils with available K <120 kg/ha.
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Foliar spray of Potassium Nitrate (13:0:45) @ 10g/L or SOP (0:0:50) @ 10g/L at weekly intervals during boll development.

visual_symptoms: Translucent yellow to orange-brown spots on leaflets of older fronds; leaflets develop severe marginal necrosis and necrotic tip drying; fronds look scorched and die prematurely.
similar_conditions: Leaf rot, Gray leaf spot (Pestalotiopsis), Tanjore wilt early yellowing.
soil_association: Coastal sands, laterites of Kerala and Karnataka with K2O <100 kg/ha.
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Apply 2 kg MOP + 1 kg Epsom Salt (Magnesium Sulphate) per palm into circular basin 1.8m from trunk.

visual_symptoms: Blossom End Rot (BER) on fruits: dark brown to black flattened sunken leathery patch at blossom end of fruit; apical leaves cup downward and margins wither.
similar_conditions: Anthracnose fruit rot, fruit borer entry holes, sunscald.
soil_association: Acidic laterite soils, sandy soils with low cation exchange capacity, dry drought-stressed soils.
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Foliar spray of Calcium Nitrate (18.8% Ca, 15.5% N) @ 5g/L or Chelated Calcium (EDTA-Ca) @ 1.5g/L during early fruit set.

visual_symptoms: Distinct interveinal chlorosis on older leaves: leaf veins remain green while interveinal tissue turns bright yellow to bronze; in severe cases leaf margins turn purple-red.
similar_conditions: Chilli mosaic virus, mite-induced stippling, early powdery mildew chlorosis.
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Foliar spray of Magnesium Sulphate @ 5g/L or 10g/L at 15-day intervals.

visual_symptoms: Khaira disease / Zinc deficiency: brownish-red or rust-colored blotches/streaks along midrib of leaves; lower leaves droop; plants severely stunted in patches.
similar_conditions: Brown spot (Bipolaris oryzae), iron toxicity bronzing, tungro virus.
soil_association: Calcareous black soils (Vertisols) of Tungabhadra, Krishna-Godavari deltas and alkaline soils of Tamil Nadu.
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Emergency foliar spray of Zinc Sulphate @ 5g/L + Lime @ 2.5g/L (or unslaked lime neutralizer) twice at 10-day intervals.

visual_symptoms: 'White Bud' of maize: broad bleached white to pale yellow bands on both sides of leaf midrib starting from base; midrib and leaf margins remain green; emerging whorl leaves almost white.
similar_conditions: Maize dwarf mosaic virus, downy mildew chlorotic stripes.
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Foliar spray of Chelated Zinc (EDTA-Zn 12%) @ 1g/L or Zinc Sulphate @ 5g/L neutralized with 2.5g lime.

visual_symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on youngest leaves: veins remain sharply green while intervening tissue becomes bleached ivory-white or pale yellow; whole cane tops appear bleached white in severe patches.
similar_conditions: Sugarcane grassy shoot disease (phytoplasma), sugarcane mosaic virus.
soil_association: Calcareous black Vertisols of North Karnataka, Western Tamil Nadu, Rayalaseema.
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Foliar spray of Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4) @ 10g/L + Citric Acid @ 1g/L (to prevent oxidation) or Fe-EDTA @ 1.5g/L twice at 10-day intervals.

visual_symptoms: Crown choking / 'Katte roga' boron deficiency: inner fronds crinkled, brittle, hook-tipped and failing to unfurl; inflorescence dries out; nut cracking and gum exudation on nuts.
similar_conditions: Yellow leaf disease, mite-induced nut cracking.
soil_association: Laterite soils of Coastal Karnataka and Kerala.
confirmation_method: Laboratory leaf tissue analysis (spectrophotometry/AAS) and soil DTPA extractable test
management: Soil application of Solubor @ 20g/palm or foliar spray with Boron 20% (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate) @ 2g/L.
source: ICAR-CPCRI Regional Station Vittal & UAS Dharwad
